record.title: Zero-distribution conjecture for Painlevé V expansion polynomials
record.statement:
For the case $l=1$, let $a_k^1(a_1^1)$ denote the polynomial coefficient in the expansion of the corresponding Painlevé V solution, and set

$$
R=\frac1{24}\sqrt{90+6\sqrt{177}}=0.5429868659\ldots.
$$

**Zero-distribution conjecture.** Every zero of every polynomial $a_k^1(a_1^1)$ lies inside the circle of radius $R$ centered at the origin of the complex plane. Numerical studies suggest this property after the largest root of $a_5^1(a_1^1)$ was computed; the source gives no proof and notes that the general $l>1$ case is left for future work.
record.source_name: F. V. Andreev and A. V. Kitaev, “Connection Formulae for Asymptotics of the Fifth Painlevé Transcendent on the Imaginary Axis: I”, arXiv:1904.06741 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06741

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2019).

record.title: Fernandes–da Cruz conjecture on simultaneous minimum t-term ranks
record.statement:
Let $R$ and $S$ be partitions of the same weight, and suppose that the class ${\cal A}(R,S)$ of matrices with row and column sums prescribed by $R$ and $S$ is nonempty. For a matrix $A$, let $\rho_t(A)$ denote its $t$-term rank, and write

$$
\widetilde{\rho}_t(R,S)=\min\{\rho_t(A):A\in {\cal A}(R,S)\}.
$$

**Fernandes–da Cruz conjecture.** If ${\cal A}(R,S)$ is nonempty, then there is a matrix $A\in {\cal A}(R,S)$ such that

$$
\rho_t(A)=\widetilde{\rho}_t(R,S)
$$

for all $t\geq 1$.

The conjecture asks whether one matrix in every nonempty class simultaneously realizes the minimum $t$-term rank for every positive integer $t$. The analogous assertion for maximum $t$-term ranks was proved, whereas this minimum-rank assertion was conjectured by Fernandes and da Cruz.
record.source_name: Rosário Fernandes, Henrique F. da Cruz and Susana Palheira, “Matrices in A(R,S) with minimum t-term ranks”, arXiv:1904.11069 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.11069

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2019).

record.title: The asymptotic almost-cover conjecture for hypercubes
record.statement:
Let $Q^n=[0,1]^n$ be the $n$-dimensional hypercube, and let $f(n,k)$ denote the minimum number of affine hyperplanes whose collection is an almost $k$-cover of $Q^n$, meaning that every vertex of $Q^n$ is covered at least $k$ times except possibly the origin.

**Almost-cover conjecture.** For an arbitrary fixed integer $k 1$ and sufficiently large $n$,

$$
f(n,k)=n+\binom{k}{2}.
$$

Equivalently, for large $n$, an almost $k$-cover of $Q^n$ contains at least $n+\binom{k}{2}$ affine hyperplanes. This is proposed for larger $k$ after the exact values are established for $k\leq 3$; the conjecture remains open in general, with the paper noting the case $k=4$ as a particular example.
record.source_name: Alexander Clifton and Hao Huang, “On almost k-covers of hypercubes”, arXiv:1904.12885 (2019).

record.statement:
Let $G$ be a fullerene graph, and let $W(G)$ denote its Wiener index. Let $C_W(G)$ denote its Wiener complexity and let $\operatorname{diam}(G)$ denote its diameter. Consider fullerene graphs of arbitrary order having maximal Wiener index.

**Wiener complexity and diameter conjecture.** The Wiener complexity and the diameter of fullerene graphs of an arbitrary order having the maximal Wiener index are given in Propositions

Together with the preceding maximal-Wiener-index claim, this conjecture aims to determine further distance-based invariants of all extremal fullerene graphs. Its validity for arbitrary order is not established by the supplied computational discussion and remains open.

record.title: Extendability conjecture for finite generalized Lyndon words
record.statement: Let $A$ be a finite alphabet, and let $w$ be a finite generalized Lyndon word over $A$. The length of $w$ is denoted by $|w|$. **Extendability conjecture.** Every finite generalized Lyndon word $w$ with $|w|\geq 2$ is a prefix of an infinite generalized Lyndon word. The conjecture identifies all finite generalized Lyndon words except the maximum one-letter word as potential prefixes of infinite generalized Lyndon words.

record.title: Packing conjecture for triple systems
record.statement:
Let $D(n,k,3)$ denote the maximum number of pairwise disjoint copies of a $K_k^{(3)}$ in a $3$-uniform complete hypergraph, and let $J'(n,k,3)$ denote the lower-bound expression used for this packing number. Let $c$ be a constant. For every integer $k$, choose an integer $n_0$, and consider integers $n\geq n_0$ satisfying

$$
(n-2)\equiv 0 \pmod {k-2},\qquad (n-1)(n-2)\equiv p(k-2)\pmod {(k-1)(k-2)},
$$

for some integer $p$ with $1\leq p\leq k-2$.

**Packing conjecture.** If $p\neq 2$, then

$$
D(n,k,3)\geq J'(n,k,3)-O(k^c).
$$

The paper proves this in all but two congruence cases, namely $k,p\equiv 4\pmod 6$ and $k,p-2\equiv 0\pmod 6$; the conjecture asserts that the lower bound has no dependence on $n$ when $p\neq 2$.
record.source_name: Ramin Javadi, Ehsan Poorhadi and Farshad Fallah, “On the packing for triples”, arXiv:1905.10807 (2019).

record.title: Alon–Hefetz–Krivelevich–Tyomkyn Poisson anti-concentration conjecture for graph edge statistics
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph. For $0\leq k\leq n$, choose a uniformly random $k$-vertex subset $A\subseteq V(G)$ and let $X_{G,k}:=e(G[A])$ be the number of edges induced by $A$. Suppose $k\to\infty$ and $n$ grows sufficiently rapidly in terms of $k$. For every integer $\ell$ with

$$
0<\ell<\binom{k}{2},
$$

**Alon–Hefetz–Krivelevich–Tyomkyn's conjecture.** One has

$$
\Pr(X_{G,k}=\ell)\leq 1/e+o(1).
$$

This conjecture seeks a Poisson-type universal upper bound, analogous to the maximum point mass of a Poisson random variable with mean one. The source gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Jacob Fox, Matthew Kwan and Lisa Sauermann, “Combinatorial anti-concentration inequalities, with applications”, arXiv:1905.12142 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.12142

record.title: Universal limiting profile for successive minimum spanning tree forests
record.statement:
For each $k\geqslant1$, let $F_k(t)$ be the forest produced by Kruskal's algorithm at time $t$, and let $\rho_k(t)$ be the limiting fraction of vertices in its largest component. The functions $\rho_k$ describe the giant-component sizes of the successive forests. **Universal profile conjecture.** There exists a continuous increasing function $\rho_\infty:(-\infty,\infty)\to[0,1)$ such that

$$
\rho_k(2k+x)\to\rho_\infty(x)
$$

uniformly in $x\in\mathbb R$ as $k\to\infty$. This predicts that the giant-component profiles become translates of one universal profile; the paper reports computational evidence, but no proof.
record.source_name: Svante Janson and Gregory B. Sorkin, “Successive minimum spanning trees”, arXiv:1906.01533 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.01533

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2019).

record.title: Sharp bounds for successive minimum spanning tree weights
record.statement:
For each $k\geqslant1$, let $\gamma_k$ be the limiting constant for the weight of the $k$th successive minimum spanning tree. **Sharp weight bounds conjecture.** For every $k\geqslant1$,

$$
2k-1\leqslant\gamma_k\leqslant2k.
$$

These bounds would sharpen the proved estimates $2k-2\sqrt{k}<\gamma_k<2k+2\sqrt{k}$ and are motivated by taking increments of the known bounds for cumulative weights; they remain unproved.

record.title: The general Turán number conjecture for disjoint cliques in multipartite graphs
record.statement:
Let $r>t\ge 3$ and $k\ge 2$, and let $n_1,\dots,n_r$ be sufficiently large. For $I\subseteq [r]$, write $m_I:=\min_{i\in I}n_i$. For a partition $\mathcal P$ of $[r]$, write $n_I:=\sum_{i\in I}n_i$ and

$$
n_{\mathcal P}:=\max_{I\in\mathcal P}\{n_I-m_I\}.
$$

**The general multipartite Turán conjecture.** The Turán number of the disjoint union $kK_t$ in the complete $r$-partite graph is

$$
\operatorname{ex}(K_{n_1,\dots,n_r},kK_t)=\max_{\mathcal P}\left\{(k-1)n_{\mathcal P}+\sum_{I\ne I'\in\mathcal P}n_In_{I'}\right\},
$$

where the maximum is over all partitions $\mathcal P$ of $[r]$ into $t-1$ parts. This conjecture seeks a general formula extending the known results for earlier cases and the paper's theorem for $r=4$ and $t=3$; its validity for arbitrary $r>t\ge3$ remains open.
record.source_name: Jie Han and Yi Zhao, “Turán number of disjoint triangles in 4-partite graphs”, arXiv:1906.01812 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.01812

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2019).

record.title: Li–Nikiforov–Schelp cycle conjecture for dense graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n\geq 4$, let $bdelta(G)$ denote its minimum degree, and write a $2$-edge-coloring as $E(G)=E(R)\cup E(B)$. Let $C_\ell$ denote the cycle with $\ell$ vertices, and say that $G$ arrows $C_\ell$ when every such coloring contains a monochromatic copy of $C_\ell$. **Li–Nikiforov–Schelp conjecture.** If 
$$
\delta(G)>3n/4,
$$
 then for all $\ell\in[4,\lceil n/2\rceil]$, $G$ arrows $C_\ell$. The paper records only a partial result for the shorter range $\ell\in[4,(1/8-\epsilon)n]$; the full assertion remains open in the supplied text.
record.source_name: József Balogh, Alexandr Kostochka, Mikhail Lavrov and Xujun Liu, “Monochromatic paths and cycles in 2-edge-colored graphs with large minimum degree”, arXiv:1906.02854 (2021).
record.references:

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.02854

record.title: The exact cardinality conjecture for largest sum-dominant subsets of an interval
record.statement:
Fix $n\geq 16$. Let $N$ be the cardinality of the largest sum-dominant subset(s) of $\{0,1,\ldots,n-1\}$ that contain(s) $0$ and $n-1$. **The exact cardinality conjecture.** Then

$$
N=n-7.
$$

The surrounding result in the paper proves only the bounds $n-7\leq N\leq n-4$; the exact equality is presented as a conjectural statement, while the paper establishes that at least four and at most seven elements must be discarded from the interval to obtain a largest sum-dominant subset.

record.title: The maximum-diamond conjecture for tournaments of order congruent to 1 modulo 4
record.statement:
Let $T=(V,A)$ be a tournament on $n\equiv 1\pmod{4}$ vertices. A **diamond** is the tournament configuration counted in the paper.

**Maximum-diamond conjecture.** The number of diamonds in $T$ is at most

$$
\frac{1}{96}(n+3)(n-1)(n-2)(n-3).
$$

This conjecture extends the preceding maximum-diamond results to tournaments whose order is congruent to $1$ modulo $4$. The supplied text does not state a resolution, so its status is open.

record.title: The newness conjecture for the maximum scattered linear set \(\mathcal{L}\)
record.statement: Let $q$ be a prime power, and let $\mathcal{L}$ denote the linear set constructed in the paper in $\operatorname{PG}(1,q^6)$. A linear set is **maximum scattered** if it is scattered and has maximum possible rank. **Newness conjecture.** The linear set $\mathcal{L}$ is a new maximum scattered linear set of $\operatorname{PG}(1,q^6)$ for each $q$ such that $q\equiv 1\pmod{4}$ and $q\not\equiv 0\pmod{5}$. This extends the computationally verified scatteredness results and the corollary establishing newness for $q\leq17$; the conjecture asserts the corresponding statement for all admissible $q$, while the general case remains open.

record.title: Domination versus edge domination in regular graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite, simple, undirected $\Delta$-regular graph with $\Delta\geq 1$. The domination number $\gamma(G)$ is the minimum cardinality of a dominating vertex set, and the edge domination number $\gamma_e(G)$ is the minimum size of a maximal matching in $G$; equivalently, $\gamma_e(G)=\gamma(L(G))$, where $L(G)$ is the line graph of $G$. **Domination versus edge domination conjecture.** For every such graph,

$$
\gamma(G)\leq\gamma_e(G).
$$

This conjecture proposes an inequality between vertex domination and edge domination for regular graphs. The equivalent line-graph formulation is $\gamma(G)\leq\gamma(L(G))$; the supplied source gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Julien Baste, Maximilian Fürst, Michael A. Henning, Elena Mohr and Dieter Rautenbach, “Domination versus edge domination”, arXiv:1906.10420 (2019).

record.title: Finiteness conjecture for optimal subvarieties in mixed Shimura varieties
record.statement: Let $M$ be a mixed Shimura variety, let $Z\subset M$ be a subvariety, and let $\delta(A)=\dim\langle A\rangle-\dim A$ denote the defect of a subvariety $A$, where $\langle A\rangle$ is the smallest special subvariety containing it. A subvariety $A\subset Z$ is **optimal** if it is maximal for its defect: whenever $A\subset B\subset Z$ and $\delta(B)\leq\delta(A)$, one has $B=A$. **Finiteness conjecture for optimal subvarieties.** For every subvariety $Z\subset M$, there are only finitely many optimal subvarieties. This is presented as formally equivalent to the strongest form of the Zilber–Pink conjecture for mixed Shimura varieties, but its status is not specified in the source.
record.source_name: Jonathan Pila and Jacob Tsimerman, “Independence of CM points in Elliptic Curves”, arXiv:1907.02737 (2019).

record.title: Conjectured analogue of the minimum-degree zero-one law for k-connectivity
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb{H}(n;\mu,K_n)$ be the inhomogeneous random K-out graph on $n$ nodes, where $0<\mu<1$, and let $k\geq2$. The sequence $K_n$ is governed by the scaling condition

$$
K_n=\frac{\log n+(k-2)\log\log n}{1-\mu}+\gamma_n.
$$

**Zero-one law conjecture for k-connectivity.** Under this scaling,

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb{P}\left[\mathbb{H}(n;\mu,K_n)\text{ is }k\text{-connected}\right]=\begin{cases}1,&\text{if }\lim_{n\to\infty}\gamma_n=+\infty,\\0,&\text{if }\lim_{n\to\infty}\gamma_n=-\infty.\end{cases}
$$

The conjecture concerns the sharp threshold for $k$-connectivity and extends the established zero-one law for minimum degree at least $k$. The footnote in the source says that this conjecture was proved by M. Sood and O. Yağan in 2019, so its database status is solved.
record.source_name: Mansi Sood and Osman Yağan, “Towards k-connectivity in Heterogeneous Sensor Networks under Pairwise Key Predistribution”, arXiv:1907.08049 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.08049

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of July 2019); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: The height bound conjecture for rational points on hyperelliptic curves
record.statement:
For an integer $d\geq 3$, let $f\in\mathbb{Q}[x]$ be a polynomial of degree $d$ with nonzero discriminant, and let $h(f)$ denote the maximum of the logarithmic heights of its coefficients. **The height bound conjecture.** There exist constants $C_1=C_1(d)$ and $C_2=C_2(d)$ such that, for every such polynomial $f$ and all $x,y\in\mathbb{Q}$ satisfying

$$
t^2=f(x),
$$

one has

$$
h(x)\leq C_1\cdot h(f)+C_2.
$$

The source presents this as a conjecture that, in degree at least $5$, follows from Vojta's conjecture over $\mathbb{Q}$; it is used to obtain infinitely many rational specializations with prescribed index-two arboreal Galois images.
record.source_name: Andrea Ferraguti, Carlo Pagano and Daniele Casazza, “The inverse problem for arboreal Galois representations of index two”, arXiv:1907.08608 (2023).

record.title: Conjecture on the injective chromatic index of subcubic graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a subcubic graph, meaning a graph with maximum degree at most $3$. The injective chromatic index, denoted by $\chi'_{\operatorname{inj}}(G)$, is the minimum number of colors in an injective edge-coloring of $G$. **Subcubic injective edge-coloring conjecture.** For every subcubic graph,

$$
\chi'_{\operatorname{inj}}(G)\leq 6.
$$

The preceding theorem gives the weaker upper bound $8$, while the complete graph supplies a lower-bound example; the proposed improvement is left unresolved in the supplied source.
record.source_name: Baya Ferdjallah, Samia Kerdjoudj and Andre Raspaud, “Injective edge-coloring of sparse graphs”, arXiv:1907.09838 (2020).

record.title: Conjecture on the injective chromatic index of subcubic bipartite graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a subcubic bipartite graph, meaning a bipartite graph with maximum degree at most $3$. Write $\chi'_{\operatorname{inj}}(G)$ for its injective chromatic index. **Subcubic bipartite injective edge-coloring conjecture.** For every subcubic bipartite graph,

$$
\chi'_{\operatorname{inj}}(G)\leq 5.
$$

The source has just established the upper bound $\chi'_{\operatorname{inj}}(G)\leq 6$ for this class, so the conjecture asks whether that bound can be decreased by one; no resolution is supplied.

record.title: Charpentier's coloring conjecture for squares of graphs with maximum average degree below 4
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $\Delta(G)$ denote its maximum degree, let $\operatorname{mad}(G)$ denote its maximum average degree, and let $G^2$ be its square, with chromatic number $\chi(G^2)$. **Charpentier's conjecture.** There exists an integer $D$ such that every graph $G$ with $\Delta(G) \ge D$ and $\operatorname{mad}(G) < 4$ has

$$
\chi(G^2) \le 2\Delta(G).
$$

The conjecture was disproved by Kim and Park, who showed that for every positive integer $D$ there is a graph satisfying the stated degree and maximum-average-degree conditions with $\chi(G^2)=2\Delta(G)+2$.
record.source_name: H. A. Kierstead, Daqing Yang and Junjun Yi, “On coloring numbers of graph powers”, arXiv:1907.10962 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.10962

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of July 2019).

record.title: Modified EGZ upper-bound conjecture for powers of $(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})$
record.statement:
Let $n$, $t$, and $d$ be positive integers. Let $s'_{nt}(G)$ denote the modified Erdős-Ginzburg-Ziv constant associated with length $nt$, and let $\ell$ be the smallest integer such that $\ell\geq 2^d$ and $\ell\nmid n$. **Modified EGZ upper-bound conjecture.** Then

$$
s'_{nt}\left((\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^d\right)\leq (t+2^d-1)n-\ell+1.
$$

This extends the preceding Berger–Wang conjecture to arbitrary positive integers $n$, $t$, and $d$; the source gives no proof or resolution.

record.title: Expanding eigenbasis conjecture for recursive eigenvector matrices
record.statement:
Let $A$ be a matrix of dimension at most $7$, and repeatedly construct eigenvector matrices $X_i$ whose columns have unit $\mathbb{L}_2$ norm. A matrix property holds for almost all matrices if, for every matrix $A$ and every $\epsilon>0$, there is a matrix $A'$ with $|A(i,j)-A'(i,j)|<\epsilon$ having that property. **Expanding eigenbasis conjecture.** For almost all matrices of dimension at most $7$, the recursively constructed matrices satisfy

$$
X_i^\dagger X_i\to I
$$

as $i$ tends to infinity. This conjecture concerns the limiting orthogonality of recursively computed eigenvectors and is supported in the paper by numerical observations and proofs for special cases; no resolution is supplied.
record.source_name: M Hariprasad, “Recursive eigen extrusion: Expanding eigenbasis conjecture”, arXiv:1907.12039 (2019).

record.title: Asplund–Fox conjecture for minimum coprime numbers of joins of paths
record.statement:
Let $P_m$ and $P_n$ be paths on $m$ and $n$ vertices, respectively, and let $\mathfrak{pr}(G)$ denote the minimum coprime number of a graph $G$. **Asplund–Fox's path-join conjecture.** For any positive integer $N$, there exists a positive integer $M$ such that for all $m>M$ and $2\leq n\leq N$, 
$$
\mathfrak{pr}(P_m+P_n)=\begin{cases}m+2n-2&\text{if }m\text{ is odd},\\m+2n-1&\text{if }m\text{ is even}.
$$
 The conjecture extends the displayed formula from the cases previously established in the source to every fixed finite range $2\leq n\leq N$ when $m$ is sufficiently large; no resolution is supplied in the provided text.

record.title: Blidia–Maffray–Zemir conjecture on the b-chromatic number of regular graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a $d$-regular graph with girth at least $5$, and let $b(G)$ denote its b-chromatic number, the largest number of colors in a b-coloring of $G$. The Petersen graph is the 3-regular graph on 10 vertices with girth 5.

**Blidia–Maffray–Zemir conjecture.** If $G$ is not the Petersen graph, then

$$
b(G)=d+1.
$$

This predicts the maximum possible b-chromatic number for regular graphs of girth at least 5, apart from the Petersen graph, and remains open.
record.source_name: Allen Ibiapina and Ana Silva, “b-continuity and Partial Grundy Coloring of graphs with large girth”, arXiv:1908.00674 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.00674

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2019). “Indeed, the following conjecture is still open.”

record.title: Bounded equitable vertex arborable threshold for planar graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple finite planar graph, and let $va^{\equiv}(G)$ denote its equitable vertex arborable threshold: the minimum integer $k$ such that $G$ admits an equitable tree-$k'$-coloring for every integer $k'\geq k$. A tree-$k$-coloring is a coloring of $V(G)$ with colors $1,2,\dots,k$ such that each color class induces a forest, and the coloring is equitable when any two color-class sizes differ by at most one. **Bounded planar equitable vertex arborable threshold conjecture.** There is a constant $C$ such that

$$
va^{\equiv}(G)\leq C
$$

for every planar graph $G$. This asks whether the equitable vertex arborable threshold is bounded independently of the size and maximum degree of planar graphs; the source provides no evidence of resolution.
record.source_name: Xin Zhang and Bei Niu, “Equitable partition of graphs into induced linear forests”, arXiv:1908.05075 (2019).

record.title: The Kővári–Sós–Turán conjecture for complete bipartite graphs
record.statement:
For a graph $H$ and an integer $n$, let $\operatorname{ex}(n,H)$ denote the maximum number of edges in a simple graph on $n$ vertices that contains no subgraph isomorphic to $H$. For positive integers $t,s$ with $t\leq s$, let $K_{t,s}$ be the complete bipartite graph with parts of sizes $t$ and $s$.

**Kővári–Sós–Turán conjecture.** For every $t,s\in\mathbb{N}$ with $t\leq s$,

$$
\operatorname{ex}(n,K_{t,s})=\Theta\left(n^{2-\frac{1}{t}}\right).
$$

This conjecture asserts that the general upper bound of Kővári, Sós and Turán gives the correct order of magnitude for every complete bipartite graph, a problem that remains open in general.

record.title: Le Brun et al.'s lunar divisor maximum conjecture in bases at least three
record.statement:
Let $b\geq 3$ and let $n$ range over the $k$-digit numbers in base $b$. Write $d_b(n)$ for the number of lunar divisors of $n$ in base $b$, and write $111\ldots 1|_b$ for the base-$b$ number with $k$ digits all equal to $1$. **Le Brun et al.'s conjecture.** Among all such $n$, $d_b(n)$ has a unique maximum at

$$
n=\frac{b^k-1}{b-1}=111\ldots 1|_b.
$$

This is a conjecture about the extremal behavior of lunar divisors; the supplied text later states and proves the equivalent result, so it is solved.
record.source_name: Gal Gross, “Maximally additively reducible subsets of the integers”, arXiv:1908.05220 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.05220

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of August 2019). “This conjecture was proved by Richard Schroeppel (, Theorem 16) and again by Frosini and Rinaldi in .”

record.title: Le Brun et al.'s binary lunar divisor maximum conjecture
record.statement:
Let $d_2(n)$ denote the number of binary lunar divisors of $n$, and let $111\ldots 10|_2$ denote the binary number with $k-1$ initial $1$'s followed by $0$. **Le Brun et al.'s conjecture.** Among all $k$-digit numbers in base $2$, the maximal value of $d_2(n)$ occurs at

$$
n=2^k-2=111\ldots 10|_2,
$$

and this is the unique maximum for $n\neq 2,4$. The supplied text does not give evidence that this conjecture has been resolved, so its status is left open.
record.source_name: Gal Gross, “Maximally additively reducible subsets of the integers”, arXiv:1908.05220 (2019).

record.title: The linkedness characterization of the two-agent price of connectivity
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a biconnected graph. For positive integers $a,b$, say that $G$ is **$(a,b)$-linked** if, for every pair of disjoint vertex sets $M_1,M_2$ with $|M_1|=a$ and $|M_2|=b$, there are disjoint connected subgraphs $G_1,G_2$ such that $M_i\subseteq G_i$ for $i=1,2$. Let $\operatorname{PoC}(G,2)$ denote the price of connectivity for two agents. **Linkedness conjecture.** If $k\geq 2$ is an integer and $G$ is $(2,k-1)$-linked but not $(2,k)$-linked, then

$$
\operatorname{PoC}(G,2)=\frac{2k-1}{2k}.
$$

The conjecture would determine the price of connectivity for the two-agent case in terms of linkedness; the paper verifies it for complete graphs with an arbitrary matching removed, but does not establish it for general biconnected graphs.
record.source_name: Xiaohui Bei, Ayumi Igarashi, Xinhang Lu and Warut Suksompong, “The Price of Connectivity in Fair Division”, arXiv:1908.05433 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.05433

record.title: Terao's minimal-degree conjecture for free line arrangements
record.statement:
Let ${\mathcal A}$ and ${\mathcal B}$ be line arrangements with isomorphic intersection lattices

$$
L({\mathcal A})\cong L({\mathcal B}).
$$

For an arrangement ${\mathcal A}$, let $r({\mathcal A})$ denote the minimal degree of a Jacobian relation. **Terao's minimal-degree conjecture.** If ${\mathcal A}$ is free, then

$$
r({\mathcal A})=r({\mathcal B}).
$$

This is presented as the line-arrangement reformulation of Terao's freeness conjecture and is open; the intersection lattice does not determine $r$ for arbitrary line arrangements.
record.source_name: Takuro Abe, Alexandru Dimca and Gabriel Sticlaru, “Addition-deletion results for the minimal degree of logarithmic derivations of arrangements”, arXiv:1908.06885 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.06885

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2019). “This conjecture is open, even in the case of line arrangements in $\PP^2$, in spite of a lot of work and partial results in the recent years, see .”

record.title: The inclusion chromatic index bound for connected graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph with minimum degree $delta\geq 2$ and maximum degree $\Delta$, and let $\chi'_{\subset}(G)$ denote its inclusion chromatic index, the least number of colours in a proper edge colouring such that the palette at every vertex is not contained in the palette at any neighbour. **Inclusion chromatic index conjecture.** If $G$ is not isomorphic to $C_5$, then

$$
\chi'_{\subset}(G) \leq \left\lceil\left(1+\frac{1}{\delta-1}\right)\Delta\right\rceil.
$$

The conjectured bound matches the lower bound supplied by the paper's infinite family of examples and would therefore be sharp. The paper proves an upper bound with an additive constant for every fixed $\delta\geq 2$, with $\frac{1}{\delta-1}$ replaced by $\frac{4}{\delta-1}$; the stated bound remains open.
record.source_name: Jakub Kwaśny and Jakub Przybyło, “On inclusion chromatic index of a graph”, arXiv:1909.00150 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.00150

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2019).

record.title: Lovász's planar graph homomorphism isomorphism question
record.statement:
Let $H$ and $H'$ be two simple graphs, possibly with loops. For every planar multigraph $G$, possibly with multiple edges but no loops, consider the homomorphism counts $\hom(G,H)$ and $\hom(G,H')$.

**Lovász's planar homomorphism question.** If

$$
\hom(G,H)=\hom(G,H')
$$

for every such planar multigraph $G$, does it follow that $H$ and $H'$ are isomorphic?

The unrestricted analogue is a theorem of Lovász, but the corresponding statement when the input graphs are restricted to planar graphs was not known in the source. This question concerns whether planar homomorphism counts determine the target graph up to isomorphism.
record.source_name: Jin-Yi Cai and Artem Govorov, “On a Theorem of Lovász that (, H) Determines the Isomorphism Type of H”, arXiv:1909.03693 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.03693

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2019).

record.title: Square-root throttling conjecture for trees
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected tree of order $n$, and let $\operatorname{th_{pzf}}(G)$ denote its probabilistic zero forcing throttling number. **Tree throttling conjecture.** The maximum possible probabilistic throttling number among connected trees of order $n$ is

$$
\Theta(\sqrt{n}).
$$

A path graph achieves the lower bound, while the corresponding upper bound for all connected trees is presented as an approachable problem toward the general square-root throttling conjecture.
record.source_name: Shyam Narayanan and Alec Sun, “Bounds on expected propagation time of probabilistic zero forcing”, arXiv:1909.04482 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.04482

record.title: The conjecture on large line-like configurations in generic norms
record.statement:
Let $||\cdot||$ be a norm whose unit circle contains neither a line segment nor an arc contained in an $L^2$ circle centered at the origin. A **line-like configuration** of size $n$ in $||\cdot||$ is a set of $n$ points whose distance graph is isomorphic to that of $n$ equally spaced points on a line.

**Large line-like configuration conjecture.** There exists $N$ such that, for every $n\geq N$, the only line-like configurations of size $n$ in $||\cdot||$ are $n$ equally spaced points on a line.

The excluded geometric features are exactly those used earlier to construct infinitely many line-like configurations. The paper reports numerical evidence for the special case of $L^p$ norms, but the general conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Sara Fish, Dylan King, Steven J. Miller, Eyvindur A. Palsson and Catherine Wahlenmayer, “Crescent configurations in normed spaces”, arXiv:1909.08769 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.08769

record.title: Uniform perturbation conjecture for motif-support size
record.statement:
Let $\degree$ be a degree sequence, and let $\psi(\degree)$ denote the number of nonzero entries of the associated multigraph representation. Define $v(\degree)$ as the smallest real number such that, for all $i$ and $j$,

$$
\left|\psi(\degree+\mathbf{e}_i+\mathbf{e}_j)-\psi(\degree)\right|\leq v(\degree).
$$

Let $u(\degree)$ be the analogous perturbation constant for $\beta$. **Uniform perturbation conjecture.** For all $\degree$, $u(\degree)\leq 1$ and $v(\degree)\leq 1$. The claim asserts uniform stability of both the parameter and the support-size statistic under adding two degree units; the supplied text provides only trivial broad bounds before stating the conjecture.
record.source_name: Philip S. Chodrow, “Moments of Uniform Random Multigraphs with Fixed Degree Sequences”, arXiv:1909.09037 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.09037

record.title: The neighbour-distinguishing index conjecture for digraphs
record.statement:
Let $D$ be a digraph. Write $\operatorname{ndi}(D)$ for its neighbour-distinguishing index and let $\Delta^*(D)$ denote the maximum of the indegree and outdegree of $D$. **Neighbour-distinguishing index conjecture.** For every digraph $D$,

$$
\operatorname{ndi}(D)\le\Delta^*(D)+1.
$$

The paper has established general upper bounds, including $\operatorname{ndi}(D)\le\Delta^*(D)+2\lceil\log k\rceil$ when the underlying graph of $D$ has chromatic number $k\geq3$, but does not resolve whether the stronger bound above holds in general.
record.source_name: Eric Sopena and Mariusz Woźniak, “A note on the neighbour-distinguishing index of digraphs”, arXiv:1909.10240 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.10240

record.title: Lu–Milans conjecture on Lubell functions of forbidden subposets
record.statement:
Let $P$ be a poset, and let $\bar{h}_n(\mathcal{F})$ denote the Lubell function of a family $\mathcal{F}$ of subsets of $[n]$. Define $\lambda_n(P)$ to be the maximum value of the Lubell function over families of subsets of $[n]$ that do not contain $P$ as a subposet. **Lu–Milans conjecture.** For every poset $P$, 

$$
\limsup_{n\to\infty} \lambda_n(P)<\infty.
$$

Lu and Milans proposed this as a general finiteness conjecture for forbidden-subposet problems. The paper states that Méroueh verified it by proving an explicit Lubell-function bound for families avoiding $B_m$ and posets of bounded 2-dimension, so this conjecture is solved.
record.source_name: Hong-Bin Chen, Yen-Jen Cheng, Wei-Tian Li and Chia-An Liu, “The Boolean Rainbow Ramsey Number of Antichains, Boolean Posets, and Chains”, arXiv:1909.11370 (2019).

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2019). “So we leave the following open problem:”

record.title: Conjecture on generalized Fibonacci growth rates below $2^n$
record.statement:
Let $M$ be an $\omega$-categorical structure with growth rate $f_M(n)$, and for $k\in\mathbb{N}$ let the generalized Fibonacci numbers be defined by

$$
F_{n,k}=\sum_{i=1}^{k}F_{n-i,k},
$$

with $F_{n,k}=0$ for $n<0$ and $F_{0,k}=1$.

**Generalized Fibonacci growth conjecture.** If

$$
f_M(n)<\frac{2^n}{p(n)}
$$

for every polynomial $p(n)$, then there is some $k\in\mathbb{N}$ such that

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}F_{n,k}^{1/n}=\lim_{n\to\infty}f_M(n)^{1/n}.
$$

The claim aims to determine the possible exponential growth constants in the range just below $2^n$; the source describes this subcase as more approachable and records the assertion as still conjectural.
record.source_name: Samuel Braunfeld, “Monadic stability and growth rates of ω-categorical structures”, arXiv:1910.04380 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.04380

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2019).

record.title: Tuza's conjecture for t-intersecting set pairs
record.statement:
Let $AK(n,k,t)$ denote the maximum size of a $k$-uniform $t$-intersecting family $\mathcal F\subseteq \binom{[n]}{k}$. Let $\{(A_i,B_i)\}_{i=1}^m$ be a collection of pairs of sets such that

$$
A_i\cap B_j=\varnothing \quad\text{if and only if}\quad i=j,
$$

and $\lvert A_i\cap A_j\rvert\ge t$ for all $i$ and $j$. Suppose that $\lvert A_i\rvert=a$, $\lvert B_i\rvert=b$, and $a\le b$. **Tuza's conjecture for t-intersecting pairs.** Then

$$
m\le AK(a+b,a,t).
$$

This is the proposed $t$-intersecting generalization of the preceding conjecture. The value of $AK(n,k,t)$ is known by Ahlswede and Khatchatrian, but the asserted inequality is not resolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Dániel Gerbner, Balázs Keszegh, Abhishek Methuku, Dániel T. Nagy, Balázs Patkós, Casey Tompkins and Chuanqi Xiao, “Set systems related to a house allocation problem”, arXiv:1910.04666 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.04666

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2019).

record.title: Baker–Shokrieh's bounded-Jacobian-exponent conjecture for biconnected graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite undirected multigraph with no self-loops. Its **Jacobian** $\mathop{\mathrm{Jac}}\nolimits\left( G \right)$ is a finite abelian group, and the **exponent** of this group is the smallest positive integer $m$ such that $ma=0$ for every $a\in\mathop{\mathrm{Jac}}\nolimits\left( G \right)$. A graph is **biconnected** if the induced subgraph formed by removing any vertex is connected.

**Baker–Shokrieh's conjecture.** For every positive integer $k$, there are only finitely many biconnected graphs $G$ such that the exponent of $\mathop{\mathrm{Jac}}\nolimits\left( G \right)$ is at most $k$.

The conjecture was made by Matthew Baker and Farbod Shokrieh. It is proved in the source for $k=2$ and $k=3$ using Dhar's burning algorithm, while the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Hahn Lheem, Deyuan Li, Carl Joshua Quines and Jessica Zhang, “Exponents of Jacobians of Graphs and Regular Matroids”, arXiv:1910.06442 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.06442

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2019).

record.title: Bounded-Jacobian-exponent conjecture for connected regular matroids
record.statement:
Let $M$ be a connected regular matroid, and let $\mathop{\mathrm{Jac}}\nolimits\left( M \right)$ denote its Jacobian, a finite abelian group. The **exponent** of this group is the smallest positive integer $m$ such that $ma=0$ for every $a\in\mathop{\mathrm{Jac}}\nolimits\left( M \right)$.

**Regular-matroid Jacobian exponent conjecture.** For every positive integer $k$, there are only finitely many connected regular matroids $M$ such that the exponent of $\mathop{\mathrm{Jac}}\nolimits\left( M \right)$ is at most $k$.

This is the regular-matroid analogue of the conjecture for biconnected graphs. The source states the analogous conjecture but does not give a resolution of it; the paper instead proves the exponent-$2$ case and characterizes all such matroids.
record.source_name: Hahn Lheem, Deyuan Li, Carl Joshua Quines and Jessica Zhang, “Exponents of Jacobians of Graphs and Regular Matroids”, arXiv:1910.06442 (2021).

record.title: Chin et al.'s edge-transitive dense graph conjecture for spanning subtrees
record.statement:
Let $G_n$ be a sequence of connected graphs, each with $n$ vertices and $Omega(n^2)$ edges, and suppose that each $G_n$ is edge-transitive. **Chin et al.'s conjecture.** Then

$$
\liminf_{n \to \infty} P(G_n)>0.
$$

Here $P(G)$ is the probability that a uniformly chosen subtree of $G$ is spanning. The conjecture is implied by the paper's theorem for graphs of minimum degree linear in $n$, so it is solved.
record.source_name: Stephan Wagner, “On the probability that a random subtree is spanning”, arXiv:1910.07349 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.07349

record.title: Three-positive-steady-state bound for the minimally bistable ERK subnetwork
record.statement: Consider the minimally bistable ERK subnetwork, and let a compatibility class be determined by the conserved quantities of the reaction system. **Three-steady-state conjecture.** For every choice of rate constants and every compatibility class, the maximum number of positive steady states is $3$. If true, the previously established no-coexistence theorem would imply that Hopf bifurcations and bistability do not coexist in compatibility classes. The bound is presented as a conjecture and remains open.
record.source_name: Carsten Conradi, Nida Obatake, Anne Shiu and Xiaoxian Tang, “Dynamics of ERK regulation in the processive limit”, arXiv:1910.14452 (2020).
record.references:

record.title: The BEV bound for linear codes in projective spaces
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb{P}_q(n)$ be the projective space of subspaces of $\mathbb{F}_q^n$, equipped with the notion of linear code introduced by Braun, Etzion, and Vardy. The **BEV bound** states that the maximum size of a linear code in $\mathbb{P}_q(n)$ is

$$
2^n.
$$

Braun, Etzion, and Vardy conjectured this as the projective-space analogue of the $2^n$ bound for binary linear block codes. The paper notes that some linear codes not closed under intersection attain this bound, while whether it holds for all linear codes remains open.
record.source_name: Pranab Basu and Navin Kashyap, “The Lattice Structure of Linear Subspace Codes”, arXiv:1911.00721 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.00721

record.title: Schröder's cop-number conjecture for graphs of bounded genus
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph, let $g(G)$ be the smallest nonnegative integer such that $G$ can be drawn on an orientable surface of genus $g(G)$ without crossing edges, and define

$$
c(g):=\max\{c(G)\mid g(G)=g\}.
$$

Here $c(G)$ is the cop number of $G$.

**Schröder's conjecture.** For every $g\in\mathbb{N}$, we have

$$
c(g)\leqslant g+3.
$$

This would improve the best known general upper bound $c(g)\leqslant\left\lfloor 3g/2\right\rfloor+3$. The conjecture is known for $g\leqslant 3$, but remains open in general.
record.source_name: Nathan Bowler, Joshua Erde, Florian Lehner and Max Pitz, “Bounding the cop number of a graph by its genus”, arXiv:1911.01758 (2019).
record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2017–2019). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1806.01821](https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.01821), [arXiv:1710.11281](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.11281).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.01758

record.title: Local version of Reed's list-coloring conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph and let $L=(L(v):v\in V(G))$ be a list-assignment. For each vertex $v$, let $d(v)$ denote its degree and let $\omega(v)$ denote the size of the largest clique containing $v$. An **$L$-coloring** is a proper vertex coloring selecting a color from $L(v)$ at each vertex. **Local version of Reed's list-coloring conjecture.** If, for every $v\in V(G)$,

$$
|L(v)| \geq \left\lceil \frac{1}{2}(d(v) + 1 + \omega(v))\right\rceil,
$$

then $G$ is $L$-colorable. This is the local analogue of Reed's conjecture and of the global list-coloring version. The paper notes that existing results give an epsilon version, while this full local statement remains open.
record.source_name: Tom Kelly and Luke Postle, “A local epsilon version of Reed's Conjecture”, arXiv:1911.02672 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.02672

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2019). “We conclude this section with an application of Theorem to Hadwiger's conjecture, which is considered one of the most important open problems in graph theory.”

record.title: The location conjecture for unique maximum absolute coefficients of q-factorials
record.statement: Let $(q;q)_n=(1-q)(1-q^2)\cdots(1-q^n)$, and let $i$ denote an exponent at which the maximum absolute coefficient of $(q;q)_n$ occurs. **Location conjecture.** For $n\geq 35$, if $n\equiv 1\pmod 4$, the absolute maximum occurs only once, as the coefficient of some $q^i$ with $i<n(n+1)/4$; if $n\equiv 3\pmod 4$, it occurs only once, as the coefficient of some $q^i$ with $i>n(n+1)/4$. This claim is based on computations and concerns the observed location of the maximum absolute coefficients for odd $n$; the source gives no proof or resolution.
record.source_name: Alexander Berkovich and Ali K. Uncu, “Where do the maximum absolute q-series coefficients of (1-q)(1-q^2)(1-q^3)(1-q^n-1)(1-q^n) occur?”, arXiv:1911.03707 (2019).

record.title: The unified difference conjecture for maximum-coefficient locations
record.statement:
For odd $n\geq 35$, define

$$
\widetilde{E}_n=2(D_n-D_{n-2}),
$$

where $D_n$ is the half-difference between the two locations of the maximum absolute coefficients of $(q;q)_n$. **Unified difference conjecture.** If $n$ is odd and $n\geq 61$, then $\widetilde{E}_n\in\{1,3\}$. The source presents this as an intriguing analogue of the earlier difference conjecture, motivated by observed data; no proof or resolution is given.
record.source_name: Alexander Berkovich and Ali K. Uncu, “Where do the maximum absolute q-series coefficients of (1-q)(1-q^2)(1-q^3)(1-q^n-1)(1-q^n) occur?”, arXiv:1911.03707 (2019).

record.title: Brešar, Klavžar, Rall, and Wаsh's packing-coloring conjecture for subdivided subcubic graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a subcubic graph, meaning that its maximum degree is at most $3$. Let $D(G)$ be the graph obtained by subdividing every edge of $G$, and let $\chi_p(G)$ denote the packing chromatic number, the smallest $k$ such that $G$ has a packing $(1,2,\ldots,k)$-coloring. **Brešar, Klavžar, Rall, and Wash's conjecture.** For every subcubic graph $G$, 

$$
\chi_p(D(G))\leq 5.
$$

The conjecture concerns a uniform upper bound on the packing chromatic number after subdividing every edge of a subcubic graph. It was motivated by an earlier question of Gastineau and Togni and was subsequently conjectured by Brešar, Klavžar, Rall, and Wash; the supplied source gives no resolution, so its status remains open.
